subject: Data handling follow-up: tailored retention & private pilot details
messages:
From: Alexandra Moss <alex.moss@synapsehealth.com>
To: ava_chen@redwoodinference.com, marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com
Cc: procurement@synapsehealth.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps — data handling & retention constraints

Hi Ava / Marcus,

Thanks again for the call earlier — appreciate the clear walkthrough of Redwood's serving options. Quick recap from our side with the asks we mentioned on the call: 

1) PII handling: we need a path that ensures no persistent storage of any clearly identified PII (names, SSNs, medical identifiers) for healthcare flows. Our legal team will only approve architectures that can demonstrate zero retention for PII tokens or a contractual carveout.

2) KV / session caching: can the platform support TTL=0 for certain request classes or disable KV cache entirely for named endpoints? If not, what operational compensations (e.g., strict redaction + ephemeral keys) are available?

3) Log/metrics retention: we typically accept aggregated metrics but require request/response logs with PII redacted and a maximum 7-day window for retained logs in the hosted environment. If the only way to meet PII constraint is a private deployment, we are open to a pilot.

4) Evidence: SOC 2 and the data flow diagrams you mentioned; our compliance team asked for proof-of-concept notes and a short playbook for how redaction/zero-ttl would be enforced.

I've attached our data classification spreadsheet for reference (synapse-data-classification.xlsx).

Next steps we want from Redwood: a short technical proposal (2 slides + one-pager) that maps options to risk (hosted + redaction, hosted + shortened logs, dedicated/private with no-KV) and an estimate of timelines and incremental cost for a 6-week private pilot.

Can we target an internal follow-up with your security lead this week? We are aiming to get procurement and legal aligned so we can move to an MSA discussion quickly if the technical fit is there.

Thanks,
Alexandra Moss
Head of Platform Security
Synapse Health
alex.moss@synapsehealth.com

From: ava_chen@redwoodinference.com <ava_chen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alexandra Moss <alex.moss@synapsehealth.com>
Cc: marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com, irene_choi@redwoodinference.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jun 2026 18:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps — data handling & retention constraints

Alexandra — thanks for the clear recap and the classification sheet (reviewing now). Short reply with proposed approach + concrete asks so we can move fast: 

TL;DR: We can support both a hosted short-logs path (7-day redacted logs) and a private/dedicated pilot that provides a zero-retention mode for PII with a contractual addendum. I'll outline both below and propose next steps.

Option A — Hosted (fastest):
- Provide endpoint-level redaction rules and automated PII masking before any persistent logs are kept.
- Log retention: configurable down to 7 days for request/response logs; metrics/aggregates kept longer.
- KV cache: cannot be fully disabled for general-purpose hosted endpoints, but we can enable a per-route no-kv flag for low-QPS, security-sensitive endpoints (this is an ops-managed configuration).
- Residual risk: short-lived in-memory caches may exist during request processing; we will describe mitigation controls in the playbook.
- Typical timeline: 1–2 weeks for configuration + compliance review. Incremental cost: small (configuration and monitoring setup).

Option B — Dedicated / Private pilot (recommended for strict PII zero-retention):
- Private control plane + customer VPC; we can run a private pool with no-kv-mode for identified routes, which prevents any KV persistence beyond the immediate process memory.
- KMS/HSM integration supported (you can bring-your-own keys).
- We will include a contractual data-retention addendum that specifies TTL=0 for PII-labeled requests and a 7-day maximum for any non-PII logs you accept.
- Typical timeline: pilot environment in 3–6 weeks depending on onboarding windows. Pricing: we will provide a dedicated pilot estimate (separate line item).

Concrete asks from Synapse for next step: 
- A sample prompt flow or two (sanitized) that shows where PII appears and the expected QPS for those endpoints.
- Confirmation whether you prefer a hosted short-logs route first or go directly to a private pilot.

I'll loop in Irene from Security to draft the technical playbook and provide the SOC 2 artifacts you requested. Attaching our internal note: redwood-zero-ttl-playbook.pdf (high level).

Proposed near-term plan:
1) Security sync with Irene — within 48 hours.
2) You send sample prompt flow + QPS numbers.
3) We deliver a 2-slide option map + pilot quote within 3 business days after the sync.

If that sounds good I'll schedule a 30-minute security touchpoint Wednesday or Thursday.

Best,
Ava Chen
Account Executive, Enterprise
Redwood Inference
ava_chen@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0187

From: irene_choi@redwoodinference.com <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Alexandra Moss <alex.moss@synapsehealth.com>, ava_chen@redwoodinference.com
Cc: marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 15 Jun 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps — data handling & retention constraints

Alexandra / Ava — appreciate the thorough summary. A few technical clarifications and what we'll need to produce the compliance artifacts you requested: 

1) Zero-retention (PII) feasibility:
- For private/dedicated deployments we can enable a strict no-kv configuration (service-level flag) that prevents any model KV state from being written to persistent storage and drops any session state on process exit.
- For hosted routes we can implement per-route masking + a short in-memory TTL but cannot guarantee 100% zero persistence due to multi-tenant operational logs. That said, we can implement a strong redaction pipeline and a 7-day retention for logs.

2) Redaction mechanics:
- We support token-level redaction and pattern-based masking pre-ingestion. We will provide a sample regex/pattern set and pre-processing steps.
- We recommend a layered approach: client-side sanitization -> server-side redaction -> request classification (PII flag).

3) Audit & evidence:
- We'll provide SOC 2 type II summary, our data-flow diagram, and a short technical playbook describing how no-kv and masking are enforced.
- For the pilot we can stand up a short runbook that captures: who can access logs, how keys are rotated, and a checklist for proofing zero retention behavior.

4) PoC suggestion:
- Run a 72-hour pilot on a dedicated node with a small traffic slice (we can mock QPS if you prefer) where we: (a) route the PII-labeled endpoints to no-kv nodes, (b) capture audit evidence showing no persisted KV, and (c) run a redaction detection test.

What we need from Synapse: 
- A sanitized example session (or two) with the PII you expect to be present and a definition of which fields must be considered sensitive.
- Your procurement and legal POC so we can draft an MSA addendum outlining TTL=0 clauses and KMS requirements.

Scheduling: I can do a 30-minute security technical sync Wed 15 Jun at 11:00 AM PDT or Thu 16 Jun at 09:00 AM PDT. Please let us know which works.

--
Irene Choi
Head of Security & Compliance (Solutions)
Redwood Inference
irene_choi@redwoodinference.com

We can get you the sanitized sample sessions by EOD tomorrow and we have legal/procurement POCs copied on this thread.
